newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Peregrine names acting Vietnam head.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine names acting Vietnam head.

text.p: Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it had named Judd Kinne acting managing director of Peregrine Capital Vietnam Ltd following the arrest of the unit's chief on tax evasion charges.

Peregrine said in a statement that it believed the charges against Nguyen Trung Truc, 44, an Australian national, related to his personal tax affairs and those of local companies with which he was associated.

"Naturally we are concerned about Mr Truc and his family and are doing everything we can to assist the Australian consulate in Ho Chi Minh City in its efforts to secure bail for him," Peregrine group legal counsel Alan Mercer said in a statement.
"Unfortunately, we have not been able to speak to Mr Truc since his arrest," he said.
Singapore-based Kinne, a director on the executive committee of Peregrine Investments, was now in Ho Chi Minh City, the Hong Kong-based investment bank said.
In February, authorities in Ho Chi Minh City had issued an Administrative Order fining Peregrine Capital Vietnam for operating a business from an unregistered office, it said.
The fine followed a nine-month investigation into the operations of Peregrine Capital Vietnam and several small local companies with which members of Truc's family were involved, it said.
Peregrine had made representations suggesting that the recommended fine of US$59,000 for operating a business from an office without a proper licence was "excessive in the extreme", Mercer said.
He added that Peregrine had considered the matter closed after the February action.
"The (latest) charges against Mr Truc were a bolt from the blue. The exact nature of the charges against Mr Truc are unclear," Mercer said.

Kinne, who established the group's securities business in Association of Southeast Asian Nation (ASEAN) countries, had been managing director of Peregrine Securities Singapore Pte since 1989, Peregrine said.

Peregrine said it had originally planned to focus on investment banking in Vietnam, but had branched out into a distribution business through local partners. However, the operation had never contributed to the group's profits, it said.
"Our Vietnam distribution business, after holding out much promise, has been a disappointment," Mercer said.
Mercer earlier told Reuters in Hanoi that the company would retreat from the distribution business and concentrate instead on project finance and investment advisory mandates.

Earlier this month, Peregrine chairman Philip Tose protested to the Bangladesh government over an order to arrest the head of a Bangladeshi company conducting business for Peregrine as part of a market-wide crackdown.
